    You said: how much sleep do adults needhow much sleep do adults need
    AI Overview

    AI Mode replied:

    Adults generally need 7 to 9 hours of sleep per night, according to the National Sleep Foundation and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. 
    Recommendations can vary slightly depending on your specific age group and individual health needs: 
    • Young adults and adults (18–64 years): Aim for 7 to 9 hours of sleep nightly.
    • Older adults (65+ years): Aim for 7 to 8 hours of sleep nightly, though individual needs may still vary.
    • Minimum threshold: Getting fewer than 7 hours of sleep on a regular basis is generally considered insufficient.⁠Mayo Clinic +2 
    Key Factors to Keep in Mind
    • Quality matters just as much as quantity: Fragmented or frequently interrupted sleep leaves you feeling unrefreshed, even if you spent enough time in bed.⁠Mayo Clinic +1 
    • Risks of chronic sleep loss: Regularly sleeping less than 7 hours is linked to serious health concerns like weight gain, high blood pressure, diabetes, heart disease, and depression.⁠Mayo Clinic 
    • Aging and sleep patterns: While older adults need about the same amount of sleep as younger adults, they often experience lighter sleep, take longer to fall asleep, and wake up more frequently during the night.⁠Mayo Clinic 
    Would you like some tips on improving your sleep hygiene, or are you trying to figure out if you're dealing with a specific sleep issue like insomnia?
